newsitem.title: UK: Dlr ends sleepy Europe session lower, markka firm.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends sleepy Europe session lower, markka firm.

text.p: The dollar slipped to the lower end of its narrow trading ranges at the European close but remained well supported on downticks, traders said.

Finland's decision on Saturday to join the European Exchange Rate Mechanism today kept the markka in firm shape and helped underpin the dollar. It had little direct impact on trading though as the move had been anticipated. A partial market holiday in the U.S. kept volumes to a minimum, traders said.
"The dollar is keeping to its familar ranges, and there has been very little volume today," said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Europe.
At 1434 GMT the dollar was at 1.5291/98 marks and 111.58/67 yen compared with 1.5311/18 and 111.66/71 in late European trading on Friday.
The Finnish markka joined the ERM at a central rate of 3.04 per mark, in line with market expectations. It last traded little changed at 2.9865/95 versus 2.9870 at Friday's close.
Dealers said the markka was likely to consolidate at current levels now after it had risen some six percent since late April.
The focus now falls squarely on Italy's lira and Sweden's crown, which along with the U.K. and Greece are the only EU countries outside the ERM.
Bubbling speculation that European Monetary Union will go ahead on time is likely to keep the mark under pressure and the dollar underpinned, analysts said.

"To the extent that Finland's move underlines the EMU process then, it should keep the mark under pressure and the dollar supported," said Joe Prendergast, foreign exchange strategist at Merrill Lynch.

Prendergast said he expected Finland to informally target 2.25-percent fluctuation bands within the ERM, which would be in keeping with the view that other ERM countries, like Spain and France, have been loosely targetting the former narrow bands.
Sterling remained firm, climbing to 20-month peaks against the mark, just shy of 2.42 marks, and hitting 11-month highs against the dollar above $1.58.

Profit-taking into the European close took the pound off its intraday peaks to $1.5790/$1.5800 and 2.4143/48 at 1452 GMT. That compared with $1.5740/50 and 2.4130/35 in late European trading on Friday.

The New Zealand dollar firmed after Saturday's election as support for left wing parties there diminished. The result was inconclusive though and uncertainty about the influence of marginal parties will cap the Kiwi's rise for now, traders said.
The New Zealand dollar was at 69.88/93 U.S. cents compared with 69.20 at the New Zealand opening earlier.
